newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower, feeders down.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower, feeders down.

text.p: CME live cattle futures finished mostly lower but showed little direction in active nearbys while feeder cattle ended at session lows on further fund liquidation and cash concerns, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.050 cent higher to 0.350 lower, with only August up and June off 0.025 at 63.750 cents a lb. Feeder cattle posted losses of 0.800 to 0.300, with August down most at 75.900 cents.
Live cattle futures found some support after falling to their lowest levels since April earlier this week. Next week's cash ideas also appear priced into the market, they said.

Shortcovering developed despite cash cattle seen trading down another $1 per cwt next week to $63 and boxed beef values slipped. Projections cash cattle prices will work lower during the summer and early indications on next week's Cattle-on-Feed report pointing to larger fed numbers also weighed on the market. Active feedlot and boxed beef movement this week encouraged some of the short covering, they added.
Early analyst projections put total onfeed cattle supplies at between 112.2 and 114 percent of a year ago as of June 1. A number at the high end would be a record high for the period, analysts said.
